question: Should workflow integrations use the existing typed plugin `session_end` lifecycle hook, or should OpenClaw add a separate internal `session:end` hook event?
rationale: Both surfaces can support completion automation, but adding an internal event expands the operator hook API while the typed plugin hook is already the current lifecycle contract and VISION.md prefers plugin-owned optional capability where the seam is sufficient.

options.title: Bless plugin `session_end`
options.body: Document typed plugin `session_end` as the supported completion hook for workflow integrations and close or retitle linked implementation attempts that do not need a new internal event.

options.title: Approve internal `session:end`
options.body: Define a narrow internal hook payload and wire it consistently across reset, delete, shutdown/restart, cron/webhook, and subagent completion paths.

options.title: Wait for linked PR review
options.body: Keep this issue open until https://github.com/openclaw/openclaw/pull/61675 is landed or closed, then reassess the remaining internal-hook gap.

recommendation.title: Bless plugin `session_end`
recommendation.body: Document typed plugin `session_end` as the supported completion hook for workflow integrations and close or retitle linked implementation attempts that do not need a new internal event.

likelyOwner.reason: The unresolved choice is primarily a hooks/plugin API-boundary decision, and this handle has the strongest current code and discussion signal for that boundary.
